recent_developments.headline: Five-year extension data presented
recent_developments.detail: Eisai and Biogen presented five-year Clarity AD extension results showing continued benefit versus natural-history comparators, including improvement on CDR-SB in 62% of the low-tau group, adding long-term evidence for early Alzheimer’s disease.

recent_developments.headline: Japan launches LEQEMBI Pen
recent_developments.detail: LEQEMBI Pen launched in Japan and entered the NHI Drug Price List, bringing weekly at-home subcutaneous treatment to patients with early Alzheimer’s disease.

recent_developments.headline: Canada reimbursement recommendation
recent_developments.detail: Canada’s Drug Agency issued a final positive recommendation supporting public reimbursement for eligible patients with MCI or mild dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease, advancing access while negotiations and provincial-plan decisions remain.

recent_developments.headline: U.S. initiation autoinjector available
recent_developments.detail: LEQEMBI IQLIK became available in the U.S. as a once-weekly 500-mg subcutaneous initiation option for early Alzheimer’s disease, enabling at-home dosing from treatment start.

recent_developments.headline: China insurance-list inclusion
recent_developments.detail: LEQEMBI was added to China’s Commercial Insurance Innovative Drug List, creating a pathway for commercial insurers to negotiate coverage and potentially expand access.

pending_decisions.decision: A CHMP opinion, or a further list of outstanding issues, on the EU variation introducing a new intravenous maintenance posology for early Alzheimer’s disease is scheduled for December 2026.

regulatory_actions.detail: Eisai’s pipeline update reported applications submitted in four additional countries for the 500-mg subcutaneous autoinjector initiation regimen for early Alzheimer’s disease.
Japan approved LEQEMBI Pen as a new subcutaneous route of administration for early Alzheimer’s disease.
China’s NMPA approved subcutaneous autoinjector initiation treatment for MCI due to Alzheimer’s disease or mild Alzheimer’s dementia.
The FDA approved a once-weekly 500-mg subcutaneous starting-dose regimen of LEQEMBI IQLIK for Alzheimer’s disease, including early disease.
The FDA extended review of the sBLA for a subcutaneous starting dose in early Alzheimer’s disease by three months after a major amendment, setting a revised PDUFA date of August 24, 2026.
NMPA granted Priority Review to the subcutaneous autoinjector application for early Alzheimer’s disease; the application had been accepted in January 2026.
The FDA accepted Eisai’s sBLA for weekly subcutaneous initiation dosing in early Alzheimer’s disease and granted Priority Review.
Eisai’s application to add an intravenous maintenance posology for early Alzheimer’s disease was accepted for review.

upcoming_catalysts.event: The CTAD LEADER symposium is scheduled to present multicenter real-world outcomes and at-home subcutaneous administration findings, informing the practicality of treatment outside trials.
CHMP is scheduled to issue either an opinion or further outstanding issues on the EU monthly IV maintenance variation, rather than a guaranteed approval.
The anticipated unextended expiry of US patent 8,025,878 is an exclusivity checkpoint subject to patent-term restoration, not a confirmed biosimilar-entry date.

differentiation: Lecanemab targets soluble Aβ protofibrils as well as insoluble aggregates, whereas Kisunla targets modified, N-terminally truncated N3pE Aβ; this mechanistic distinction does not establish comparative clinical superiority.
US Leqembi Iqlik enables at-home treatment from initiation with 500 mg subcutaneously once weekly, whereas Kisunla requires IV administration every four weeks.
Leqembi supports continued maintenance after 18 months, including 360 mg subcutaneously weekly, contrasting with Kisunla’s option to stop treatment after amyloid plaque clearance.
risks: ARIA and potentially fatal intracerebral hemorrhage remain material safety constraints, with symptomatic ARIA-E occurring in 9% of treated ApoE ε4 homozygotes versus 2% of heterozygotes and 1% of noncarriers.

The average randomized benefit was modest at 0.45 CDR-SB points over 18 months, while subcutaneous efficacy relies on bridging to IV evidence and long-term maintenance benefit remains incompletely established.
Ongoing dosing and MRI monitoring may constrain persistence and uptake against Kisunla’s monthly, potentially finite treatment course.
The March 2027 unextended core-patent expiry creates exclusivity uncertainty because BioArctic’s March 2032 projection assumes a five-year extension where available.
content.summary: Leqembi (lecanemab) is Eisai’s approved anti-Aβ protofibril antibody for early Alzheimer’s disease, with IV treatment and US at-home subcutaneous initiation and maintenance options. In Clarity AD, it reduced 18-month CDR-SB worsening by 0.45 points versus placebo, representing 27% relative slowing. The central question is whether easier administration and sustained treatment can translate that modest average benefit into durable real-world use despite ARIA risk, monitoring requirements and competition from potentially finite treatment.
